name: Boötes I Dwarf
tagline: The 'dim champion' — an ultra-faint Milky Way satellite 197,000 light-years out, discovered in SDSS data in 2006.
history: Boötes I appeared in 2006 as an overdensity of old stars in Sloan survey fields — an ultra-faint dwarf barely distinguishable from a stray globular cluster except for its huge physical extent and its dark-matter-dominated internal velocities. It belongs to the generation of dwarfs so faint that surveys are still finding them; each one tests how few stars a halo can gather and still count as a galaxy.
